novelty_flags.label: Theorems 1--2
novelty_flags.one_line: tier=letter below novelty_target=field: the closest omitted comparison is BellegoBenatiaDortetBernadet2025 Corollaries 1--2 and equations (17)--(22), which already make pair-selection reweighting central; establish a strict survey-design/cohort-recovery extension rather than present the factorization as a new correspondence theorem.

novelty_flags.label: Proposition 1
novelty_flags.one_line: The proposed witness makes every observed and every untreated outcome equal to the lower endpoint, with all distinguishing variation hidden in missing treated potential outcomes; replace it with a non-degenerate parametric family or generic obstruction.

soundness_flags.label: ass:link-parallel-trends; Theorems 2--3
soundness_flags.one_line: The model invokes an undefined 'declared chain', while Theorem 2 quantifies over every supported chain; parallel trends is assumed only on the unspecified declared chain, so the universal-chain assertion is not licensed.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 1
soundness_flags.one_line: The phrase 'complete sufficient calibration' is unquantified: q being constant is sufficient for a fixed outcome law, whereas covariance-zero is the stated iff; state the intended uniform-over-m_a condition explicitly if constancy is meant to be necessary.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorems 1--2
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Population ATT identification is conditional on externally available or separately identified rho and on error-free cohort recovery plus link-specific MAR.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The pair-weight and chained-DiD equalities hold only under those stated longitudinal-correspondence conditions.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 3
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Sharpness is conditional on a defensible known finite outcome support and parallel trends along a precisely fixed chain.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The LP interval is sharp only within the bounded-support audit model after that chain is specified.

source_verification_receipts.version: Corrected author copy, 20 January 2025; cited Journal of Econometrics primary was inaccessible for full-text inspection.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper explicitly handles sample selection on observables and past outcomes by reweighting the probability of a two-wave observed link conditional on covariates, treatment group, and prior outcome.
The paper studies unconditional moments with MAR data and an augmented inverse-probability-weighted moment system.
The article studies efficiency and identification for moment restrictions with missing data and auxiliary data, including known or unknown missing-data probabilities.

source_verification_receipts.version: NBER Technical Working Paper 230; page lists the published Econometrica 69(6), 2001 version.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Refreshment samples can test attrition models and identify a class of nonignorable missing-data models without strong functional-form assumptions.
The paper identifies staggered-DiD causal parameters under parallel trends, including covariate-conditioned versions, and develops estimation and inference.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Introduction, paragraphs beginning 'To the best of our knowledge' and 'This paper contributes generally'.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies DiD with a misclassified treatment, distinguishes point identification under one-sided error from complementary ATT bounds under two-sided error, and notes the link to repeated-cross-section DiD treatment-status missingness.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Agricultural Economics advance online publication, DOI 10.1111/1477-9552.70067.
source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3.2, paragraphs at lines 188--193; Section 4, line 201.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article states that annual small-firm sampling yields an unbalanced panel, expresses confidence in sampling independence, uses sampling weights, says firms can be tracked, and says missing observations are imputed using expectations of remaining firm observations; it also describes complete coverage above 50 employees and representative sampling below it.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Book overview and contents, especially Missing Outcomes chapter, pp. 6--25.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The book develops nonparametric partial identification with explicit sampling-process assumptions and includes missing-outcome analysis.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define one fixed chain as a model input, make every theorem quantify over that chain only, and state a separate theorem if parallel trends is strengthened to every supported link.

Compare directly to BellegoBenatiaDortetBernadet2025 Corollaries 1--2: prove a strict extension driven by known survey-design pair probabilities, linkage, and cohort recovery, or recast the result as an application audit informed by that paper.
Replace the endpoint-only Proposition 1 witness with a non-degenerate generic family preserving positive outcome variation and demonstrate observational equivalence throughout that family.

To clear the field floor, add a result that partially identifies or recovers cohort ascertainment or joint response/linkage probabilities under stated paradata restrictions, rather than assuming them in the positive identification theorem.

recommended_next_step: Revise on this angle: repair the chain quantification, establish a strict distinction from chained-DiD pair-selection weights, and supply a non-degenerate audit obstruction before advancing to Stage 0.
